title: Unsupervised anomaly detection in brain MRI via disentangled anatomy learning
core_idea: Introduce a reconstruction framework for unsupervised brain MRI anomaly detection that separates anatomy from imaging-specific information using a disentangled representation module (constrained by brain anatomical priors and a differentiable one-hot encoding operator) and then restores high-quality pseudo-healthy images via an edge-to-image restoration module that reconstructs anatomy from high-frequency edge cues and recouples imaging information to suppress abnormal residuals and preserve structural details.
tldr: A two-module method that decouples anatomical structure from imaging factors and reconstructs pseudo-healthy MRIs from edge-derived anatomical representations to improve unsupervised detection of brain anomalies across modalities and centers.
